description: The physics of the universe. Covers stellar structure and evolution, compact objects, galaxies, cosmology, and the application of all prior physics and mathematics to understanding celestial phenomena.

concepts.title: The Celestial Sphere and Coordinate Systems
learning_objectives: Describe the equatorial and ecliptic coordinate systems for locating celestial objects
Convert between coordinate systems using spherical trigonometry
Explain sidereal time, hour angle, and the relation between observer location and visible sky

concepts.title: The Magnitude System and Electromagnetic Spectrum
learning_objectives: Define apparent and absolute magnitude and convert between them using the distance modulus
Relate magnitude differences to flux ratios using Pogson's equation
Describe the electromagnetic windows of the atmosphere and the rationale for multi-wavelength astronomy

concepts.title: Distance Measurement: The Cosmic Distance Ladder
learning_objectives: Explain parallax and compute stellar distances from parallax angles
Describe standard candles (Cepheids, Type Ia supernovae) and their role in the distance ladder
Apply the distance modulus m − M = 5 log(d/10 pc) to compute distances

concepts.title: Telescopes and Detectors
learning_objectives: Describe the principles of reflecting and refracting telescopes and their resolving power
Explain the operation of CCD detectors and their quantum efficiency
Discuss the principles of radio, infrared, and X-ray astronomy instrumentation

concepts.title: Blackbody Radiation in Astrophysics
learning_objectives: Apply the Planck function, Wien's law, and Stefan-Boltzmann law to stellar radiation
Estimate stellar surface temperatures from peak wavelength or color indices
Compute stellar luminosity from surface temperature and radius: L = 4πR²σT⁴

concepts.title: Atomic Spectra and Spectral Line Formation
learning_objectives: Explain the formation of absorption and emission lines from atomic energy transitions
Apply selection rules to determine which transitions produce spectral lines
Describe line broadening mechanisms: natural, thermal (Doppler), and pressure broadening

concepts.title: Spectral Classification and the HR Diagram
learning_objectives: Classify stars by spectral type (O, B, A, F, G, K, M) and luminosity class
Explain the physical basis for the spectral sequence in terms of temperature and ionization
Plot and interpret the Hertzsprung-Russell diagram, identifying the main sequence, giants, and white dwarfs

concepts.title: The Doppler Effect and Radial Velocities
learning_objectives: Apply the Doppler formula (classical and relativistic) to compute radial velocities from spectral line shifts
Describe how radial velocity measurements reveal binary stars and exoplanets
Explain the cosmological redshift and its distinction from the kinematic Doppler shift

concepts.title: Visual and Spectroscopic Binary Systems
learning_objectives: Classify binary systems as visual, spectroscopic, eclipsing, or astrometric
Apply Kepler's third law to determine total mass from orbital period and semi-major axis
Extract individual masses from radial velocity curves of double-lined spectroscopic binaries

concepts.title: Eclipsing Binaries and Stellar Radii
learning_objectives: Determine stellar radii from the timing of eclipses in eclipsing binary light curves
Compute the surface temperature ratio from the depth of primary and secondary eclipses
Discuss the mass-luminosity relation for main sequence stars

concepts.title: Mass Transfer and Interacting Binaries
learning_objectives: Describe Roche lobe geometry and the conditions for mass transfer in close binaries
Classify mass transfer types (wind accretion, Roche lobe overflow)
Explain the role of mass transfer in novae, X-ray binaries, and Type Ia supernovae

concepts.title: Hydrostatic Equilibrium
learning_objectives: Derive the equation of hydrostatic equilibrium dP/dr = −ρg from force balance
Estimate central pressure and temperature using the virial theorem
Explain the interplay between gravity and pressure that determines stellar structure

concepts.title: Energy Transport: Radiation and Convection
learning_objectives: Derive the radiative transport equation in terms of opacity and temperature gradient
State the Schwarzschild criterion for convective instability
Describe the structure of convective and radiative zones in low-mass and high-mass stars

concepts.title: Nuclear Energy Generation
learning_objectives: Explain the mass-energy equivalence E = mc² as the source of stellar energy
Describe the proton-proton chain and CNO cycle for hydrogen fusion
Calculate energy release per reaction using nuclear binding energies and mass defect

concepts.title: The Equations of Stellar Structure
learning_objectives: State the four equations of stellar structure: mass conservation, hydrostatic equilibrium, energy transport, and energy generation
Describe the boundary conditions at the center and surface of a star
Explain how stellar models are constructed numerically from these equations

concepts.title: Star Formation
learning_objectives: Derive the Jeans mass and Jeans length for gravitational collapse of a gas cloud
Describe the stages of protostellar collapse from molecular cloud to T Tauri star
Explain the role of angular momentum conservation and magnetic fields in star formation

concepts.title: Main Sequence Evolution
learning_objectives: Explain the main sequence as the locus of hydrogen-burning stars in the HR diagram
Relate main sequence lifetime to stellar mass: t_MS ∝ M/L ∝ M^{−2.5}
Describe the evolution of chemical composition and structure during main sequence burning

concepts.title: Post-Main-Sequence Evolution of Low- and Intermediate-Mass Stars
learning_objectives: Describe the subgiant, red giant, horizontal branch, and asymptotic giant branch phases
Explain the helium flash and subsequent helium burning (triple-alpha process)
Describe planetary nebula ejection and white dwarf formation

concepts.title: Massive Star Evolution and Supernovae
learning_objectives: Describe successive nuclear burning stages (H, He, C, Ne, O, Si) in massive stars
Explain the iron core collapse mechanism for core-collapse supernovae
Describe the role of neutrinos in core-collapse supernovae and the formation of neutron stars

modules.title: Compact Objects: White Dwarfs and Neutron Stars

concepts.title: White Dwarfs and Electron Degeneracy
learning_objectives: Explain electron degeneracy pressure as the support mechanism for white dwarfs
Derive the mass-radius relation for white dwarfs using the Fermi gas model
State the Chandrasekhar limit (~1.4 M☉) and its derivation from relativistic degeneracy

concepts.title: Neutron Stars and Pulsars
learning_objectives: Describe the internal structure of a neutron star (crust, neutron superfluid, core)
Explain the pulsar mechanism as a rotating magnetic dipole emitting beamed radiation
Apply conservation of angular momentum and magnetic flux to predict neutron star properties

concepts.title: Black Holes: Classical Theory
learning_objectives: Derive the Schwarzschild radius R_s = 2GM/c² from escape velocity arguments
Describe the spacetime geometry around a non-rotating black hole (Schwarzschild metric)
Explain the event horizon, gravitational redshift, and time dilation near a black hole

concepts.title: Accretion and High-Energy Astrophysics
learning_objectives: Derive the Eddington luminosity as the maximum luminosity supported by radiation pressure
Describe accretion disk structure and the conversion of gravitational energy to radiation
Explain the observational signatures of X-ray binaries and active galactic nuclei

concepts.title: Interstellar Gas and Dust
learning_objectives: Describe the phases of the interstellar medium (molecular, cold neutral, warm, hot)
Explain interstellar extinction and reddening due to dust
Compute column density from 21-cm hydrogen line observations

concepts.title: HII Regions and Ionization Equilibrium
learning_objectives: Derive the Stromgren radius from the balance between ionization and recombination rates
Describe the emission spectrum of HII regions and forbidden line transitions
Estimate the temperature and density of nebulae from emission line ratios

concepts.title: Structure and Kinematics of the Milky Way
learning_objectives: Describe the components of the Milky Way: disk, bulge, halo, and spiral arms
Analyze the rotation curve of the galaxy and derive enclosed mass from V(R)
Explain differential rotation and Oort's constants

concepts.title: Dark Matter Evidence from Galactic Rotation Curves
learning_objectives: Compare observed flat rotation curves to the Keplerian prediction for visible mass
Estimate the mass of the dark matter halo from rotation curve fitting
Discuss additional evidence for dark matter (gravitational lensing, CMB, large-scale structure)

concepts.title: Galaxy Morphology and Classification
learning_objectives: Describe the Hubble sequence (elliptical, spiral, lenticular, irregular galaxies)
Relate galaxy morphology to star formation rate, gas content, and dynamics
Explain the surface brightness profiles: de Vaucouleurs law for ellipticals, exponential disk for spirals

concepts.title: Active Galactic Nuclei and Quasars
learning_objectives: Describe the unified model of active galactic nuclei (Seyferts, quasars, blazars)
Explain how supermassive black hole accretion powers AGN luminosity
Discuss the Eddington limit, jet formation, and feedback effects on the host galaxy

concepts.title: Galaxy Evolution and Mergers
learning_objectives: Describe hierarchical structure formation in the ΛCDM framework
Explain the role of galaxy mergers in morphological transformation
Discuss the evolution of the galaxy luminosity function and star formation rate density over cosmic time

concepts.title: The Equivalence Principle and Curved Spacetime
learning_objectives: State the weak and strong equivalence principles
Describe spacetime as a curved manifold and geodesics as free-fall trajectories
Interpret the metric tensor as encoding distances and time intervals in curved spacetime

concepts.title: Einstein's Field Equations and the Schwarzschild Solution
learning_objectives: State Einstein's field equations G_μν = (8πG/c⁴)T_μν conceptually
Describe the Schwarzschild metric as the vacuum solution for a spherical mass
Derive the classical tests of GR: perihelion precession, light deflection, gravitational redshift

concepts.title: Gravitational Waves
learning_objectives: Describe gravitational waves as ripples in spacetime propagating at the speed of light
Derive the quadrupole formula for gravitational wave emission (order of magnitude)
Explain the LIGO detection of binary black hole and neutron star mergers

concepts.title: The Cosmological Principle and the FRW Metric
learning_objectives: State the cosmological principle (homogeneity and isotropy on large scales)
Write the Friedmann-Robertson-Walker metric and identify the scale factor a(t)
Relate the cosmological redshift to the scale factor: 1 + z = a(t₀)/a(t_emit)

concepts.title: The Friedmann Equations
learning_objectives: Derive the Friedmann equations from Einstein's field equations for a homogeneous universe
Define the critical density, density parameter Ω, and the deceleration parameter
Solve the Friedmann equations for matter-dominated, radiation-dominated, and dark-energy-dominated universes

concepts.title: Hubble's Law and the Age of the Universe
learning_objectives: State Hubble's law v = H₀d and describe measurements of the Hubble constant
Calculate lookback time and the age of the universe for different cosmological models
Describe the observational evidence for the expansion of the universe

concepts.title: Dark Energy and the Accelerating Universe
learning_objectives: Describe the Type Ia supernova evidence for accelerating cosmic expansion
Introduce the cosmological constant Λ as a dark energy candidate and its equation of state w = −1
Discuss the ΛCDM model as the concordance cosmology and its parameters

concepts.title: The Hot Big Bang and the Cosmic Microwave Background
learning_objectives: Describe the thermal history of the universe from the Planck epoch to recombination
Explain recombination, decoupling, and the origin of the cosmic microwave background (CMB)
Interpret the CMB blackbody spectrum and its temperature T = 2.725 K

concepts.title: Big Bang Nucleosynthesis
learning_objectives: Describe the synthesis of light elements (H, He, Li) in the first few minutes after the Big Bang
Relate the predicted helium mass fraction (~25%) to the baryon-to-photon ratio
Compare BBN predictions to observed primordial abundances as a test of cosmology

concepts.title: Inflation
learning_objectives: Describe the horizon, flatness, and monopole problems of standard Big Bang cosmology
Explain how a period of exponential expansion (inflation) resolves these problems
Describe how quantum fluctuations during inflation seed the large-scale structure of the universe

concepts.title: CMB Anisotropies and the Power Spectrum
learning_objectives: Describe the angular power spectrum of CMB temperature fluctuations
Explain the physical origin of acoustic peaks from baryon-photon oscillations
Extract cosmological parameters (Ω_m, Ω_b, Ω_Λ, H₀) from the CMB power spectrum

concepts.title: Large-Scale Structure and the Matter Power Spectrum
learning_objectives: Describe the growth of density perturbations from the Jeans instability in an expanding universe
Define the matter power spectrum P(k) and relate it to galaxy survey observations
Explain baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO) as a standard ruler for cosmological distances

concepts.title: Gravitational Lensing
learning_objectives: Derive the gravitational lens equation and the Einstein ring radius
Distinguish between strong lensing, weak lensing, and microlensing
Describe how weak lensing surveys map the distribution of dark matter

concepts.title: Exoplanets: Detection and Characterization
learning_objectives: Describe the radial velocity and transit methods for exoplanet detection
Compute planet mass and radius from radial velocity and transit observations
Discuss the habitable zone and atmospheric characterization via transmission spectroscopy

concepts.title: Multi-Messenger Astronomy
learning_objectives: Describe the complementary information from gravitational waves, electromagnetic radiation, neutrinos, and cosmic rays
Explain the GW170817 neutron star merger as a landmark multi-messenger event
Discuss how multi-messenger observations constrain the neutron star equation of state and the origin of heavy elements

concepts.title: Dark Matter Candidates and Detection
learning_objectives: Classify dark matter candidates (WIMPs, axions, sterile neutrinos, primordial black holes)
Describe direct detection experiments and their sensitivity to WIMP-nucleon interactions
Discuss indirect detection through annihilation products and collider searches

concepts.title: Open Problems: Dark Energy, Quantum Gravity, and the Multiverse
learning_objectives: Discuss the cosmological constant problem and the discrepancy with quantum field theory predictions
Describe the hierarchy of approaches to quantum gravity (string theory, loop quantum gravity)
Outline the observational tests that could distinguish between dark energy models

projects.title: Building an HR Diagram from Stellar Data
projects.description: Using a catalog of stellar observations (magnitudes, colors, parallaxes), construct an HR diagram. Identify the main sequence, giant branch, and white dwarf sequence. Estimate ages of open clusters by isochrone fitting.
learning_objectives: Convert apparent magnitudes and colors to absolute magnitudes and temperatures
Plot and interpret an observational HR diagram
Estimate cluster age by fitting theoretical isochrones to the main sequence turnoff

projects.title: Modeling Stellar Structure with the Lane-Emden Equation
projects.description: Solve the Lane-Emden equation numerically for polytropic stellar models. Compare density, pressure, and temperature profiles for different polytropic indices and relate them to physical stellar models.
learning_objectives: Derive the Lane-Emden equation from the equations of hydrostatic equilibrium and a polytropic equation of state
Solve the Lane-Emden equation numerically for n = 0, 1, 1.5, 3, and 5
Relate polytropic models to real stellar structures (white dwarfs, convective stars)

projects.title: Measuring the Hubble Constant from Simulated Supernova Data
projects.description: Given simulated Type Ia supernova apparent magnitude and redshift data, fit a cosmological model to determine the Hubble constant and the matter/dark energy density parameters. Construct a Hubble diagram and analyze residuals.
learning_objectives: Construct a Hubble diagram (redshift vs. distance modulus) from supernova data
Fit cosmological parameters (H₀, Ω_m, Ω_Λ) using chi-squared minimization
Analyze residuals to assess evidence for an accelerating universe

projects.title: Extracting Cosmological Parameters from the CMB Power Spectrum
projects.description: Analyze a simplified CMB angular power spectrum. Identify the positions and heights of acoustic peaks and use them to estimate the baryon density, matter density, and spatial curvature of the universe.
learning_objectives: Relate acoustic peak positions to the sound horizon and angular diameter distance
Estimate Ω_b from the ratio of odd to even peak heights
Estimate Ω_total from the position of the first peak and discuss spatial curvature
